chunks: From him, from Sa'dan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:

I asked him about the swords adorned with silver, which are sold for gold until a specified term. He said: 'The people did not differ regarding women (in marriage) that it is riba (usury); they only differed regarding hand-to-hand (exchange).'
I said to him: 'And we sell it for dirhams (silver coins) with immediate payment?' He said: 'My father used to say: It is more pleasing to me that there be a commodity (goods) with it.'
I said to him: 'If the dirhams given are more than the silver contained in the sword?' He said: 'How can they be cautious regarding that?'
I said: 'Indeed, they claim that they know that.' He said: 'If they know that, then there is no harm; otherwise, it is more pleasing to me that they include a commodity with it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the preferred method for selling silver-adorned items for gold on credit to avoid riba?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* addresses the specific fiqh of selling silver-adorned swords for gold on credit, highlighting the scholarly distinction between *riba al-nasi'ah* (interest on delay) and *riba al-fadl* (excess in exchange). The Imam advises including a commodity (*'ard*) alongside the currency to mitigate uncertainty in valuation, reflecting the Shia emphasis on precaution (*ihtiyat*) in commercial transactions to ensure validity.
